title: Ideal H1 vanishing implies H1 vanishing for finite free kernels
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that H¹(X,J)=0 for every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf J⊆O_X [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. For every finite index type I and every O_X-linear map p: O_X^(I) → O_X, the kernel F of p satisfies H¹(X,F)=0. No surjectivity of p, cover, quasi-compactness, or affineness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering, kernel filtration paragraph; its filtration argument does not require the map to be surjective

proof.text: Choose an enumeration of the finite index type. Finite free modules and O_X are quasi-coherent. The kernel F of p is quasi-coherent by quasi-coherent kernel closure. For each j, identify F_j with the kernel of the restriction of p to the first j summands, so every F_j is quasi-coherent and F_0=0.

The projection F_j → O_X to the last coordinate has kernel F_(j-1). Its image J_j is quasi-coherent by quasi-coherent image closure, and is an O_X-submodule of O_X, hence a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. On affine opens its section ideals commute with localization, and thus give IdealSheafData; its associated toModules is isomorphic to J_j. The first isomorphism theorem gives a short exact sequence 0 → F_(j-1) → F_j → J_j → 0.

The additive cohomology functor sends F_0=0 to zero. Apply the full long exact cohomology sequence to each preceding short exact sequence. In H¹(F_(j-1)) → H¹(F_j) → H¹(J_j), the left term vanishes inductively and the right term vanishes by the ideal hypothesis, transported along the ideal-module isomorphism. Exactness forces every element of the middle term to be zero. Induct to j=|I|. This also covers an empty index type, when F=0.

theorem finite_free_kernel_h1_zero (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hI : ∀ (I : X.IdealSheafData), I.toModules.IsQuasicoherent →
      Subsingleton ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace 1).obj I.toModules))
    {I : Type u} [Finite I]
    (p : SheafOfModules.free (R := X.ringCatSheaf) I ⟶
      SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) :
    Subsingleton ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace 1).obj (kernel p))
